Diet and fracture healing: evidence-aware review: 3

A patient with diabetes has persistently elevated glucose during fracture recovery. He asks whether merely avoiding one dessert guarantees normal healing. Which broader metabolic issue should be assessed instead of treating a single food choice as sufficient?

  1. Assessment and management of diabetes
  2. Adequate protein and micronutrient intake
  3. Appropriate mechanical stability
  4. Adequate blood supply
  5. Individualized medication review
Answer and explanation

Assessment and management of diabetes

Diabetes and persistent hyperglycemia are relevant systemic factors; blaming one food alone misses overall metabolic control.

Option explanations

Assessment and management of diabetes: Diabetes and persistent hyperglycemia are relevant systemic factors; blaming one food alone misses overall metabolic control.

Adequate protein and micronutrient intake: Healing needs adequate nutrition; correcting deficiency is more defensible than promising benefit from excessive supplementation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Appropriate mechanical stability: Nutrition cannot compensate for inadequate fracture stability. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Adequate blood supply: Biological healing requires viable perfused tissue as well as mechanical support. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Individualized medication review: The risks and benefits of medicines during healing should be reviewed; prescribed drugs should not be stopped indiscriminately. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
